title: Soul-glass a Personality Test RPG
author: Mrbuttshaman
selftext:
I used Claude to make this game last week.  I programmed, modeled, made my own artwork, fiddled with Unity, Godot, and Unreal engine unsuccessfully for years.  I had a bunch of the assets sitting on my computer from some failed game dev ambitions before AI became a thing which I used here.  I gave Claude access to my asset folder, worked with it to create a game design document, I have it quiz me on things its unsure about in general to make sure it aligns on what I'm trying to achieve, then once I went through that, I had it generate and present concept art using my comfy\_ui workflow for which I made design decisions.  I then had it write up the script which I reviewed and discussed changes with.  There were ALOT of issues on the first build with collision, tile placements, tile applications, sometimes the dialogue didn't match was going on, or asked you to do things that were impossible or there were no visual indicators of what to do, sometimes you spawned in walls and it didn't save your progress so if something broke, you couldn't progress. 

Anyway, I did this all in about 2 hours for the base game and probably another 4 hours to playtest and clean up the bugs.  I tested it with some friends and added an export option as they had requested for their results.  

Overall, I'm pretty happy with it for a throwaway project.  It was inspired by Ultima 4's intro quiz and Dragon Warrior 3's intro quiz.  I have some more serious stuff I'm working on with AI but its still pretty early so I'm not quite ready to share it more widely yet.

  
Anyway, let me know what you think and potentially share what you got from the quiz.  One note, this is expected to be around a 1 hour to 2 hour playthrough, you can play on mobile and on the desktop and save if you don't want to do it all at once.

replies.author: Mrbuttshaman
replies.body: Thanks, I certainly thought so.  This was something I had bouncing around in my head since I played these type of games as a kid and I messed around with rpg maker and clickteam fusion back in the day but I just never really succeeded at it.  I think its so cool these tools exist to bring our visions to reality.

replies.author: clydeagain
replies.body: Word!! I want to truly make a game that I want to play and share with others. I'm thinking I'll have visual descriptions of items and personalities for NPCs with some contexts and let AI drive the chat lines and flavor texts so that I can also discover and learn about them. And without AI, this wouldn't be possible because a game dev already knows every single aspect of the game that they developed.

replies.author: Mrbuttshaman
replies.body: I actually started out using AI to basically roleplay anime isekai because I definitely liked that.  I would give it character archetypes to introduce and the general plot and let it fill in the details.  For this project, I kind of approached it from the same place but structured around a personality test and with actual art assets since I had most of them and was able to generate the rest.
